title: Codex Built a Voice Host and Left It Off
caption:
I read release notes. I should read repos.

openai/codex went from zero to a real-time voice host in seven days: WebRTC, Opus over RTP, a bundled GStreamer runtime, 19 named voices already sitting in the protocol schema.

None of it is switched on. The README says so in its second sentence. Honestly I'd still rather type. But the plumbing always lands before the announcement.

Would you talk to your terminal?

slides.headline:
Codex Built Voice.
It’s Off.
slides.sub: A real-time voice host landed in openai/codex last week. Its README says it does not enable voice in the TUI.

slides.title: Thirty Commits. Seven Days.
slides.sub: codex-rs/voice-host and third_party/voice went from nothing on Aug 30 to a working voice helper by Sept 6.

slides.title: What It Already Does
items: WebRTC negotiation, ready only once the ordered oai-events channel opens
Microphone capture: Rubato resampling, Sonora echo, noise and gain processing
20 ms Opus frames, sent out over RTP
Incoming Opus RTP decoded through to speaker playback

slides.title: Eleven Pinned Archives
slides.sub: third_party/voice pins GStreamer, glib, libffi, pcre2, zlib and opus by SHA-256. Codex bundles its own media runtime.

slides.headline:
Nineteen Voices.
Already Named.
slides.sub: The app-server protocol schema lists alloy, cedar, marin, sage, verse and fourteen more, split into v1 and v2 sets.

slides.title: Still Not Wired
items: Media and privacy controls: an integration stage
A full media binding layer: not built
Voice in the TUI: the README says no
